topology: Eight inches of uniform lossless 50 Ω line; no discontinuity or stub, CTLE off.
planes: 50 Ω input/output wave-reference planes; group delay before CTLE.

evidence.provenance: First-principles boundary conditions, linear circuit laws or the declared teaching-loop equation; no measured or licensed data.

checks.derivation: A matched lossless two-port has |S21|=1, so 20 log10|S21|=0.
Eight inches × the declared 170 ps/in propagation delay = 1360 ps.
The discrete impulse weights sum to the unity DC transfer under this FFT convention.

lesson.prediction: Can a channel have zero insertion loss while still delaying the signal?
lesson.experiment: Open the scenario, keep its network and stimulus fixed, and inspect the stated observation. Compare with the derived answer before changing one variable.
lesson.explanation: Yes. The ideal transfer is exp(−jωτ): magnitude is unity and group delay is τ. Bulk-delay removal changes the impulse time reference, not the input/output group delay.
lesson.transferQuestion: Does changing symbol rate change the physical delay of this fixed lossless line?
lesson.answer: No. The delay in seconds is unchanged; its length in unit intervals changes.

limitations: Ideal matched lossless model, not a real copper channel.
Group delay is checked at every exported frequency, not only its mean.
Do not compare the peak of individual discrete impulse weights with unity gain.
stimulus: Frequency sweep and discrete impulse of a matched lossless channel; fixed PRBS/edge pipeline retained by the lab.
